source.title: The Platonic Universe: Do Foundation Models See the Same Sky?
source.authors: UniverseTBD;  :; Trinidad Borrell; Steven Dillmann; Kshitij Duraphe; Furkan Eris; Kartheik Iyer; Ashod Khederlarian; Aman Kumar; Giovanni Marraffini; Michael J. Smith; Shashwat Sourav; Rocco Di Tella; John F. Wu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It identifies itself as published at ICLR 2027; no truncation affecting the reported results is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper explicitly tests representation alignment with scale using MKNN, a measure it says follows the original PRH methodology, on new model families and settings. It also adds CKA and astronomy-specific cross-modal comparisons.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many linear-probe physics results that do not themselves measure representation alignment; those are not rows. Rows below cover the alignment measures, their relationships to probe performance, scaling results, and the intervention on the probe-defined subspace. The study fixes MKNN k=10; it does not vary k.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether alignment rises with model capability, using the PRH's own measure (mutual k-NN, k=10), on a basket of vision, VLM and astronomy models over matched galaxy observations. It also contrasts MKNN with CKA, which bears on V6, and runs a subspace-removal intervention and a DINOv3 teacher/basket analysis, which bear on V7's account of the causes.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that local (MKNN) but not global (CKA) alignment tracks physics performance, supporting the Aristotelian over the strict Platonic hypothesis, and that DINOv3 and PaliGemma show parameter count alone does not predict convergence. They also claim the subspace intervention gives causal evidence that shared astrophysical content drives alignment. They argue the HSC–DESI result shows convergence is not due to input statistics or shared image pretraining.
record.recipe_differences: Uses MKNN following the original PRH methodology, with permutation calibration and fixed k=10; adds CKA and uses matched astronomical observations plus physical-property probes rather than the original study's settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported result depends on the similarity measure: MKNN trends are generally positive while CKA trends are usually absent. DINOv3 and PaliGemma differ from the main pattern. MKNN uses k=10 throughout; k is not varied.

fits_no_version.finding: A single model's embeddings of the same galaxies under different instruments align more (MKNN, not CKA) as its probe R² rises. This holds after controlling for family and parameter count. PaliGemma 28B is an exception, with lower alignment alongside lower R².
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within one model, representations of the same objects seen through different sensors align more as the model is more capable.

fits_no_version.finding: The pairwise cosine relations among redshift, stellar-mass and sSFR probe directions are similar across models and match known astrophysics (Fig. 3, Figs. 8–9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different models encode shared physical variables in a similarly organised linear subspace.

record.problems: Cross-modal sample sizes are uneven; only three physical properties are probed; cross-architectural analysis is restricted to the 1.67k JWST-HSC sample. DINOv3 checkpoints confound distillation with other training differences. MKNN k is fixed, so sensitivity to k is not assessed. The paper notes incidental galaxy exposure may be possible in internet-derived pretraining corpora.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix D.1 Table 5 reports per-checkpoint DINOv3 teacher and basket MKNN scores; those are summarized by the explicitly stated increasing-teacher/decreasing-basket trends in r24–r25 rather than expanded into separate rows for every checkpoint. Appendix F Table 7 lists individual per-checkpoint cross-modal values; the reported PaliGemma negative scaling result is recorded in r26, while the full checkpoint-level table values are not transcribed.

untested.parts: Language-only models and non-astronomy inputs. Within-family tests share architecture and data. Most cross-architecture evidence is a correlation with probe R² on 1.67k galaxies.
All: no image–caption or vision–language paired alignment is measured.
All: no mapping, stitching or relative representations.
All: no neuron, SAE-feature or circuit matching.
Sensitivity to k (fixed at 10), other measures beyond MKNN/CKA, and out-of-distribution inputs.
Plateau with scale. Whether shared pretraining data explain alignment is argued only indirectly (Specformer, App. B), not tested by control.

missing.what: Absolute alignment levels. Cross-modal MKNN is about 0.5–16%. Within-family MKNN is about 4–52% (Legacy/HSC often below 15%), while CKA is often above 60%. These bear on V7's claim that alignment stays far from complete.
missing.locator: App. E Table 6; App. F Table 7

missing.what: Per-property cross-architecture results. HSC CKA vs redshift R² is significant (ρ=0.513, p=0.009), an exception to the CKA null. HSC MKNN vs mass is only borderline (ρ=0.385, p=0.06).
The DINOv3 7B teacher's basket alignment is lower than that of the small students (HSC 17.6, JWST 19.4).
Per-property intra-family and cross-modal results. MKNN is significant for all three properties; CKA is not significant except DESI (p≈0.03–0.04).
missing.locator: App. E Fig. 11; App. F Fig. 12

record.verdict_notes: Rows comparing one model's embeddings of two instruments were relinked to none, since V1 concerns alignment between different models. The binomial scale counts (r20–r22) pool those same-model cross-modal pairs with intra-family pairs. The reader's V7 'supports' label for the intervention was wrong: that result argues against V7's alternative-cause account, and only modestly (7% MKNN drop). The authors' 'CKA null across all four tests' sits uneasily with the 21% CKA drop under the intervention and the DESI borderline result. k is fixed at 10, so V6's k-dependence is untested.

versions.untested_parts: Tests scale and probe-performance relationships using astronomy models and modalities. Does not establish that convergence holds for all architectures, tasks, data, or modalities.
No vision-language alignment of paired images and their captions is measured; the cross-modal comparisons are astronomical observations of the same galaxies.
Does not compare training seeds or test shared features/subspaces across independently initialized same-architecture networks.
Does not test linear mapping, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
Does not identify recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Compares local MKNN with global CKA, but fixes k=10 and does not systematically vary metric settings or evaluate out-of-distribution inputs.
Reports incomplete/local-only patterns and model-specific exceptions. It does not directly test whether shared training data or objectives explain the alignment, nor demonstrate a general plateau.
